```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(zetaGDUM)
```

## Data

```{r data}
sim <- simulate_metacommunity(n_sites = 80, n_species = 80, seed = 1)
dim(sim$comm)
```

## Zeta curve, retention rate and breakpoint

```{r curve}
cur <- zeta_curve(sim$comm)
zeta_break(cur)
head(zeta_curve(sim$comm, type = "abundance"), 4)
```

## Which species an order represents

```{r weights}
w2 <- zeta_weights(sim$comm, 2)
w8 <- zeta_weights(sim$comm, 8)
c(species_with_weight_k2 = sum(w2 > 0), species_with_weight_k8 = sum(w8 > 0))
```

## Turnover and nestedness for sets of sites

```{r sets}
idx <- sample_sets(80, 4, M = 500, seed = 1)
head(zeta_sets(sim$comm, idx), 3)
```

For more than two sites these components describe species shared by every site, so
replacement among subsets can be missed. Species can instead be attributed exactly
to the *total* set-level response:

```{r contributions}
inc <- species_contributions(sim$comm, idx, "presence")
rel <- species_contributions(sim$comm, idx, "relative")
head(inc$response)
head(rel$response)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(rowSums(inc$dissimilarity), inc$response)))
```

The relative response uses proportions within each non-empty site. The existing
balanced-variation and Bray--Curtis-type responses use raw counts, so they also
reflect differences in total abundance. Similarity weights and species-level
response contributions answer different questions; neither is an exact
decomposition of fitted GDUM coefficients.

## Multi-site GDUM across orders

```{r orders}
res <- zeta_orders(sim$comm, sim$env, sim$coords, M = 2000, ndraw = 20,
                   groups = list(env1 = "env1", env2 = "env2", distance = "distance"))
res
compare_orders(res, "importance")
compare_orders(res, "shapley")
```
